Nizhyn Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Chernihiv Oblast, Ukraine

Not demolished. Nizhyn holds a site of major significance to Chabad Hasidism: Dov Ber of Lubavitch, son of Shneur Zalman of Liadi — founder of Chabad-Lubavitch, documented at Hadyach elsewhere in this collection — died and was buried here in 1827, making Nizhyn one of the movement's centers in Ukraine. The town's Jewish population grew to 7,631 (23.8 percent) by 1897, and the community withstood pogroms in 1881, 1905, and 1919, the last of which, carried out by Denikin's Volunteer Army, killed about 200 Jews, including Rabbi Shlomo Menachem Hein. Nizhyn was the birthplace of three notable Jewish cultural figures: Soviet actor and singer Mark Bernes (born Menakhem-Man Neumann, 1911); Yiddish-language poet Mani Leib (born Mani Leib Brahinsky, 1883); and American theatre artist Boris Aronson. Only 16 Jews are known to have survived the Holocaust in Nizhyn.
